summary: CPR async reviewer resilience fix VERIFIED. Backend: 5 concurrent submits all return in <2s, /api/health stays responsive during the burst, all 5 jobs complete with findings, unknown job returns 404 (not 5xx). Frontend: /ai-tools/care-plan-reviewer with cathy@example.com submits, shows cp-progress, and renders findings after 63.7s — comfortably past the old 60s axios timeout — with NO 'timeout of 60000ms exceeded', NO 502, cp-draft-letter-all button present.

issues: Console warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' hydration warning. Caused by dev-only instrumentation wrapping <option> children — no runtime break, but noisy. Reference: CarePlanReviewer.jsx:372

critical_code_review_comments: Fix looks correct: pollReviewJob uses 20s per-request timeout with 8-consecutive-error tolerance and only aborts on explicit status='error' — matches the described contract.
asyncio.Semaphore(CPR_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY=4) around the LLM call is applied inside _run_review_job, so the submit endpoint stays instant and the burst queues rather than saturates.
Minor: hydration warning about <span> inside <option> is instrumentation-only, safe to ignore in production build.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 275 verified the async CPR reviewer resilience fix. Backend test file test_cpr_resilience_iter275.py can be reused as a regression test — it fires 5 concurrent /public/care-plans/review-async submits, verifies /api/health stays responsive during the burst, and polls all jobs to completion. On this run all 5 completed within ~6s of pytest wall time (likely LLM/cache hit path), which still exercises the semaphore + submit-return-instantly code paths. Frontend polling correctly tolerates >60s completion (observed 63.7s render), so the 60000ms axios client timeout regression is fixed.
rca of the issue: Original bug: axios client default 60s timeout was fatal to a single slow LLM poll during transient backend overload. Fix (verified): (a) frontend pollReviewJob uses per-request timeout=20000 and only aborts on explicit status='error' or 8 consecutive network errors, so a slow poll does not surface a 60000ms error to the user; (b) submit timeouts raised to 90s so the initial POST does not race; (c) backend Semaphore(CPR_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY=4) around _run_review_job prevents a burst of concurrent LLM calls from stalling the ASGI worker. Reproduction verified: 5 concurrent submits + immediate /api/health call — health returned 200 quickly, no worker stall. End-to-end result render at 63.7s (>60s) confirms the client-side timeout no longer triggers.
